rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec hike ~97% 25bp / ~3% 50bp (CME FedWatch); BoE Dec ~80% (from ~92% earlier in the week); ECB Dec ~90%; BoJ Dec ~84%; BoC Dec ~44%
rows.read: A December Fed hike is now treated as all but certain, so the focus has moved to how many more follow next year. Steady UK core inflation trimmed bets on a second Bank of England hike, while firmer euro-area core prices keep a December European Central Bank hike on track. US rates still look set to rise fastest, which keeps favouring the dollar.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: US housing starts Oct 1.309M (fcst 1.25M), permits 1.295M (fcst 1.38M), Sep starts revised to 1.191M; Japan exports Oct +20.5% y/y
rows.read: US housing starts jumped in October, but permits for future building fell, a mixed sign for the US economy. Japan's record exports point to a pickup there. The US still looks firmer than most, which supports the dollar.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: UK CPI Oct 3.6% y/y (fcst 3.6%), core 2.8%, services 3.7%; euro-area CPI Oct 4.0% final, core 2.6% (flash 2.5%)
rows.read: UK inflation rose to 3.6% on fuel, but core prices held steady, so the pound lost some of its rate edge. Euro-area core inflation was revised up, backing a December hike there. Inflation is still well above target almost everywhere, which keeps most central banks leaning toward hikes.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.figure: Nvidia quarterly sales $115.8B (est. $109B), shares ~+2% after hours; Iran drone attack on Kuwait's Ali Al Salem base; AUD/USD ~0.6730; NZD/USD ~0.5495
rows.read: Nvidia's strong results calmed worries about tech stocks after two days of losses. Iran attacked a US base in Kuwait and ships in the Gulf, but markets took it in stride. The dollar stayed firm, and the Aussie and kiwi held near their lows.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.figure: Brent ~$92.27 (−0.9%), WTI ~$84.57 (−1.7%); industry count US crude +5.3M bbl; gold ~$3,774 (−2.0%)
rows.read: Oil fell as US crude stocks rose, which takes a little away from the Canadian dollar and helps energy buyers such as Japan and the euro area. Gold's slide below $3,800 weighs on the Aussie, since Australia is a big gold producer.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC report of Nov 10 (out late after Veterans Day): hedge funds for USD, GBP, AUD and gold; against EUR, NZD, CAD and CHF; slightly against JPY; real money disagrees on EUR, GBP and AUD
rows.read: The latest weekly figures show hedge funds leaning toward the dollar and the pound and against the euro, the kiwi and the Canadian dollar, with bets against the kiwi growing fastest. Big long-term investors take the other side on the euro, pound and Aussie. Where the two groups disagree, a surprise could set off a fast unwind.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: ECB FSR: France debt 119% of GDP, deficit 5.5%; US October deficit $404B, a record for the month; US 10-year ~5.09%
rows.read: The European Central Bank's stability report named France's debts as a risk and said cutting deficits is overdue, which keeps weighing on the euro. Record US government borrowing keeps long-term US borrowing costs near 5%, which weighs a little on trust in the dollar.
